elements.content: Grammar focus: Can, Could, Be Able To.

Decide the time first. Present: can. General past skill: could. One specific past success: was able to. Future or perfect: be able to with the tense. Negative forms follow the same logic.

can — present ability and possibility: she can run the audit
could — general past ability: he could read at four
was able to / managed to — single past achievement: we were able to finish
will be able to — future ability: we will be able to start on Monday
have been able to — ability up to now: they have been able to cope
couldn't / wasn't able to — past inability: they weren't able to finish
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'Next year we ___ expand the team.'
2. Complete: 'Despite the storm, they ___ land safely.'
3. Which sentence is wrong?
options: I have been able to do it.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

She can run the audit alone. — Present ability. (Can has no other forms.)
He could read at four. — General past ability. (Could for past skill.)
We will be able to start on Monday. — Future ability. (Be able to carries the tense.)
What do you observe?

Can covers present ability and possibility but has no infinitive, perfect or future forms. Could covers general past ability; for a single achievement in the past, use was able to or managed to. Be able to supplies every tense can lacks: will be able to, have been able to, would like to be able to.
1. Which form is used for a single past achievement?
2. Which form supplies the future?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can make polite requests.

Success criteria:
- I can use can and could for present and past ability.
- I can use was able to for a single achievement.
- I can use be able to for future and perfect forms.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ We will can start on Monday (can has no future form) → ✅ We will be able to start on Monday
❌ We could finish the audit yesterday (could for a single achievement) → ✅ We were able to finish the audit yesterday
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The team will be able to report by June.
They managed to close the gap in one quarter.
We have been able to hold the price.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where have to, must, should, had better carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Have To, Must, Should, Had Better. Decide the strength first: obligation, advice or warning. Then decide the source: the speaker (must), an institution (have to), or nobody in particular (should). Keep mustn't apart
Can you already use this?

- I can use can and could for present and past ability.
- I can use was able to for a single achievement.
- I can use be able to for future and perfect forms.
